title: Mean as a balance point
line: Seven dots sit on a seesaw number line, and the pivot slides back and forth until it balances exactly at the mean, 6.

title: One outlier drags the mean
line: A tenth dot flies out to 95, dragging the mean marker far to the right while the median marker barely twitches.

title: Mean distance, laid end to end
line: Each dot drops a segment to the mean, the segments line up end to end, then split evenly into the MAD.

title: Dot plot becomes a box plot
line: Fifteen dots split at the median and quartiles, then a box and whiskers grow around them as the dots fade away.

title: Dots melt into a histogram
line: Twenty stacked dots slide into bins of width 5 and fuse into solid bars, turning a dot plot into a histogram.

title: Same mean, different spread
line: Two rows of five dots both balance at 10, then one row stretches outward while its mean marker stays frozen.

title: Nine values, one number
line: Nine dots slide together and merge into a single dot at their mean, then a bracket grows back out showing their spread.

title: Dice sums build a hill
line: Two dice roll again and again, each sum dropping a dot above 2 through 12, until a triangle-shaped pile peaks at 7.

title: Dragging out a tail
line: A symmetric hill of dots gets pulled one dot at a time to the right until it leans with a long right tail.

title: Taxi fare table becomes a line
line: Rows of a taxi fare table, 3 dollars plus 2 per mile, fly onto axes as dots until a straight line appears.

title: Filling tank, climbing graph
line: Water fills a tank at 4 liters a minute while a dot climbs beside it, tracing y = 4x as the tank rises.

title: Every number bigger than 3
line: Dots land at 3.5, 4, 10, 3.01 and more, packing tighter until they melt into a solid arrow from an open circle.

title: Open circle or closed
line: A point creeps toward 5 under x < 5 and the circle stays hollow, then the sign becomes ≤ and the circle fills in.

title: Balance scale algebra
line: A mystery box and 3 weights balance 8 weights, 3 come off each side, and the box is left balancing 5.

title: Tape diagram for 4x = 28
line: A 28-unit bar splits into 4 equal pieces, then one piece lifts out and its length counts up to 7.

title: x is every number at once
line: The letter x flickers through 1, 2, 3, 4 while 3x + 1 beside it updates, one expression covering every case.

title: Perimeter of any square
line: A square grows and shrinks with side s, and its perimeter 4s counts along as a dot traces the border.

title: Testing candidates
line: Numbers 1 through 6 drop into 2x + 3 = 11, each wrong one bouncing off red until 4 locks in green.

title: A trail of true values
line: A point slides from 0 to 6 while the inequality glows green then red, leaving a green trail that becomes the solution set.

title: Always the same number
line: 3(x + 2) and 3x + 6 sit side by side while x spins through 0, 1, 5, and 12, and both outputs always match.

title: Fooled by one value
line: 2x and x² both give 4 when x is 2, then x slides to 3 and the match breaks apart: 6 versus 9.

title: Distributing with a rectangle
line: A 3 by (x + 2) rectangle splits into a 3x piece and a 6 piece, so 3(x + 2) becomes 3x + 6.

title: Sorting like terms
line: Scattered tiles for x + 3 + 2x + 1 slide into two piles, x tiles with x tiles and ones with ones, giving 3x + 4.

title: Order of operations tree
line: 2 + 3 × 4² collapses one step at a time as a tree, exponent first, then times, then plus, ending at 50.

title: Celsius to Fahrenheit machine
line: Temperatures 0, 20, and 100 drop into a machine labeled F = 9C/5 + 32 and come out 32, 68, and 212 on a thermometer.

title: Doubling by folding
line: A square splits in half, then every piece splits again, ten times over, while a counter climbs 2, 4, 8 up to 1024.

title: Three cubed from three squared
line: A 3 by 3 grid of dots shows 3², then two more copies slide in beside it to make 3³ = 27 dots.

title: Counting steps across zero
line: A dot walks from (−3, 2) to (4, 2) one step at a time while a counter ticks to 7, which is 3 + 4.

title: Rectangle across four quadrants
line: Four points, one in each quadrant, connect into a rectangle, and each side length pops out from its coordinates as a brace.

title: Absolute value as distance
line: Points at −6 and 4 each stretch a band back to 0, then the bands lie side by side and −6's is longer.

title: Bigger but less
line: 10 > 2 on a number line, then both points flip to −10 and −2, swapping order as the inequality sign flips too.

title: Opposite of the opposite
line: A point at 3 flips over 0 to −3, then flips again and lands back on 3 as −(−3) = 3 writes itself.

title: Signs flip, point reflects
line: Point (2, 3) mirrors across the y-axis to (−2, 3), then across the x-axis to (−2, −3), its signs changing as it lands.

title: Two number lines make a plane
line: A number line copies itself, the copy swings up to vertical through 0, and a grid fills in to make the coordinate plane.

title: Sea level is zero
line: A vertical number line becomes the sea: a diver sinks to −20, a gull rises to 15, and 0 is the waterline.

title: GCF by chopping squares
line: A 24 by 36 rectangle chops off the biggest squares it can, until 12 by 12 squares tile the leftover exactly: GCF 12.

title: Two frogs meet at the LCM
line: Two frogs hop along a number line, one by 4s and one by 6s, until both land on the same spot at 12.

title: Pulling out a common factor
line: 36 dots and 8 dots each arrange into rows of 4, then join into one block showing 36 + 8 = 4(9 + 2).

title: Decimal multiplication as area
line: A 1.3 by 2.4 rectangle on a grid breaks into ones, tenths, and hundredths pieces that add up to 3.12.

title: Long division as sharing
line: 672 blocks get shared among 3 groups: hundreds split first, leftovers break into tens and ones, and each group ends with 224.

title: How many 3/4s fit in 2
line: Copies of a 3/4 bar slide along a 2-unit bar: two fit, and the leftover 1/2 is 2/3 of another, so 2 2/3.

title: Dividing by 1/3 triples
line: A 2-unit bar gets chopped into thirds and the piece count climbs to 6, then into fifths and it climbs to 10.

title: Double number line
line: Miles and hours number lines stretch in lockstep, 60 above 1, 120 above 2, as a slider finds 150 above 2.5.

title: Thirty out of a hundred
line: A 10 by 10 grid fills 30 squares, then rearranges onto a row of 50 people and 15 of them light up.

title: Finding the whole from 40%
line: A bar worth 12 is marked 40%, splits into four 3s, then six more 3s appear and the whole reads 30.

title: Price of one apple
line: A $6 bag of 4 apples splits open into 4 single apples, the price tag splitting with them into four $1.50 tags.

title: Which bag is the better deal
line: Bags of 5 for $3 and 8 for $4.40 each shrink down to one item, revealing 60 cents against 55 cents.

title: Three to two, forever
line: Three red and two blue squares copy themselves into rows, 6 to 4, then 9 to 6, while the color mix never changes.

title: Same shade of green
line: A cup mixes 2 scoops of blue with 3 of yellow; doubling both keeps the exact green, but one extra blue darkens it.

title: Box net, face by face
line: A flat net of six rectangles lights one face at a time, each area counting into a running surface area total.

title: Pyramid net petals
line: A square base with four triangle flaps: each flap swings out flat, its area adds to the base, and the total counts up.

title: Polygon from coordinates
line: Six points drop onto a grid and connect into an L-shaped hexagon, and each side length is read off by subtracting coordinates.

title: Parallelogram into rectangle
line: A triangle slices off one end of a parallelogram and slides to the other end, making a rectangle with equal base and height.

title: Triangle is half a parallelogram
line: A triangle gets a copy that spins 180 degrees and snaps on, forming a parallelogram exactly twice its area.

title: Trapezoid doubled
line: A trapezoid with bases 3 and 7 copies itself, flips, and joins to make a parallelogram with base 10, so half of that.

title: Three coin flips as a tree
line: A coin flip branches into H and T three times, and the 3 of 8 leaves with exactly two heads light up.

title: Double sixes in 36 cells
line: A 6 by 6 grid of dice pairs fills in, then only one corner cell lights up for double sixes: 1 in 36.

title: Spinner versus the tally
line: A spinner split 1/2, 1/4, 1/4 spins 40 times while bars of real counts wobble near the predicted heights.

title: Catching a loaded die
line: A die rolls 60 times, bars grow, one face towers over the rest, and the fair 1/6 model gets crossed out.

title: Coin flips settle down
line: A coin flips 500 times while a graph of the fraction of heads swings wildly at first, then settles onto 0.5.

title: Raindrops estimate pi
line: Random dots rain onto a square with a circle inside, and the fraction landing in the circle creeps toward 0.785, which is π/4.

title: From impossible to certain
line: Events slide onto a 0 to 1 line: rolling 7 on one die at 0, heads at 1/2, sunrise at 1.

title: Swapping marbles
line: Ten marbles swap from red to blue one by one while a pointer on a 0 to 1 line tracks the chance of red.

title: Sun plants versus shade plants
line: Two dot plots of plant heights stack up, mean markers drop onto each, and the gap between them reads 5 cm.

title: Pulling two piles apart
line: Two matching dot plots start on top of each other, then one slides right while the gap counts up in MADs: 1, 2, 3.

title: Sample results pile up
line: Twenty random samples of 10 beads are scooped from a jar, and each sample's percent red drops as a dot, piling up near 40%.

title: A biased scoop
line: From a grid of 100 dots, a sample grabbed from one corner shows 90% blue, while a scattered random sample shows the true 60%.

title: Running the machine backward
line: x passes through times 3, then plus 5, and comes out 20; the arrows reverse and carry 20 back to 5.

title: Dividing by a negative
line: Solving −2x > 6, both sides divide by −2, the number line mirrors across 0, and the solution arrow flips to x < −3.

title: A 5% raise is 1.05a
line: A bar of length a gets a 5% sliver glued to its end, then the whole bar relabels from a + 0.05a to 1.05a.

title: Zero pairs vanish
line: Tiles for 2x + 3 and −x − 5 pile together, opposite tiles pair up and vanish with a pop, leaving x − 2.

title: Factoring 6x + 9
line: Six x tiles and nine unit tiles regroup into 3 identical rows of 2x + 3, so 6x + 9 becomes 3(2x + 3).

title: Negative times negative
line: −3 times 3, 2, 1, 0, −1 gives dots at −9, −6, −3, 0, then 3, climbing by 3 each time, forcing a positive.

title: Why 1/7 repeats
line: Long division of 1 by 7 runs on screen, the remainders cycle 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, and the digits 142857 loop forever.

title: Adding as an arrow
line: An arrow for −8 snaps onto a number line starting at 5 and ends at −3, then a +8 arrow carries it straight back.

title: Subtracting is adding the opposite
line: 7 − 3 and 7 + (−3) play out as arrows on two number lines side by side and finish at the same spot.

title: Distance is the difference
line: Points at −4 and 3 have a brace between them reading 7, and as both points slide around, the brace keeps matching |a − b|.

title: 20% off, then 20% on
line: A $100 bar shrinks 20% to 80, then grows 20% to 96, falling short because the second 20% is of a smaller bar.

title: Straight through the origin
line: Points for 3 cups of flour per 2 eggs line up through (0, 0), while points for y = 2x + 1 miss it.

title: Unit rate at x = 1
line: A dot slides along y = 2.5x to x = 1, and a dashed line drops to show the unit rate 2.5 sitting right there.

title: Half mile, quarter hour
line: A walker covers 1/2 mile in 1/4 hour, then the trip copies itself 4 times along the track: 2 miles per hour.

title: One L-shape, three ways
line: An L-shaped floor is cut across, cut down, then seen as a 6 by 5 rectangle minus a corner: 26 every time.

title: Vertical angles stay twins
line: Two crossing lines turn while the opposite angles of the X show matching readouts, 50 and 50, then 70 and 70.

title: Sweeping across a straight line
line: A ray sweeps across a straight line, one angle growing as the other shrinks, and their sum stays stuck at 180.

title: Circle into a rectangle
line: A circle cut into 16 wedges rearranges into a near-rectangle of width πr and height r, so the area is πr².

title: Rolling out pi
line: A circle with diameter 1 rolls along a number line, its rim leaving a trail that ends just past 3.14.

title: Peeling rings into a triangle
line: A circle's thin rings peel off, straighten into strips, and stack into a triangle with base 2πr and height r.

title: Sticks that can't close
line: Sticks of 3, 4, and 9 swing on hinges but never meet, then the 9 shrinks to 6 and the triangle snaps shut.

title: One swing, two triangles
line: A side of length 5 swings from a fixed corner and crosses the base line in two places, giving two different triangles.

title: Double scale, four times floor
line: A 2 by 3 room plan doubles to 4 by 6, and exactly four copies of the original slide in to fill it.

title: Bike ride as a graph
line: A rider goes out, stops, and comes home while a distance graph draws beside it: steep when fast, flat when stopped, falling back.

title: Filling a flask
line: Water fills a flask with a narrow neck, and the height graph bends upward as the level speeds up in the neck.

title: Two points make a line
line: Points (2, 7) and (5, 13) get a rise-over-run staircase of slope 2, then the line extends back to hit the y-axis at 3.

title: Burning candle
line: A 12 cm candle shrinks 1.5 cm each hour beside a graph whose line starts at 12 and hits zero at hour 8.

title: Equal steps or growing steps
line: y = 2x and y = x² plot together, and equal steps right give equal climbs for one and bigger climbs for the other.

title: Dialing m and b
line: In y = mx + b, dialing m from −2 to 3 tilts the line, then dialing b slides it up and down without turning.

title: A table races a graph
line: Runner A is a table and runner B is a graphed line; both race on a track and B overtakes at second 4.

title: One input, one output
line: Inputs drop into a machine and each pops out one output, then a broken machine spits two outputs for one input and turns red.

title: The vertical line test
line: A vertical line sweeps across a parabola touching it once each time, then across a sideways parabola where it hits twice.

title: Two-way table in percents
line: A table of 100 students by pet and phone fills in, then each row converts to percents and the rows clearly differ.

title: Reading the trend line
line: Plant heights by week get the line y = 2x + 3, a slider at week 7 reads 17 cm, and the 3 means starting height.

title: Spin the line to fit
line: A line rotates through a scatter plot while vertical gaps to each point stretch and shrink, and a total-gap counter bottoms out.

title: Scatter plots that change shape
line: A cloud of points morphs from rising, to falling, to no pattern, to a curve, with a label appearing for each shape.

title: Where two lines cross
line: Lines y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 7 draw on axes, a dot rides each one, and the two dots meet at (2, 5).

title: Parallel, then the same line
line: Two lines with slope 3 never meet, then one slides its intercept until it merges with the other, giving infinitely many solutions.

title: Three ways an equation ends
line: Three equations simplify side by side and land on x = 4, then 5 = 5, then 3 = 7, each ending glowing a different color.

title: Expand, collect, solve
line: 3(x + 2) = x + 14 expands, x terms slide left and numbers slide right, until it shrinks to x = 4.

title: Slope triangles anywhere
line: A rise-run triangle slides along y = 2x + 1, stretching as it goes but staying similar, so rise over run always reads 2.

title: Slope is the price per pound
line: On the graph of $4 per pound, a step of 1 right and 4 up repeats into a staircase hugging the line.

title: Multiplying in scientific notation
line: (3 × 10⁴)(2 × 10⁵) splits apart, the 3 and 2 multiply, the exponents add, and 6 × 10⁹ assembles.

title: Powers of ten zoom out
line: A number line zooms out tenfold each step, from 1 to 10 to 100 all the way to 10⁹, as the exponent ticks up.

title: Building a million dots
line: A 10 by 10 grid of dots shrinks into one dot of a new 10 by 10 grid, three times over, reaching a million.

title: Square roots as sides
line: Squares of area 1, 4, 9, 16 line up by side length, then a square of area 2 squeezes in between 1 and 2.

title: Swinging the diagonal down
line: The diagonal of a unit square swings down onto a number line like a compass arm and lands at 1.414.

title: Exponents add by counting
line: 2³ × 2⁴ unpacks into three 2s and four 2s, the times sign dissolves, and seven 2s regroup into 2⁷.

title: Why 2⁰ is 1
line: A column of 16, 8, 4, 2 halves at each step down, so 2⁰ lands on 1 and 2⁻¹ lands on 1/2.

title: Closing in on √2
line: A zoom box narrows from 1.4 to 1.5, then 1.41 to 1.42, trapping √2 one digit at a time on a number line.

title: Ordering π, 3.15, and √10
line: π, 3.15, and √10 drop onto a number line near 3, and a zoom reveals the order: π, then 3.15, then √10.

title: 0.2727... becomes 3/11
line: x = 0.272727... copies itself as 100x, the endless tails line up and cancel, leaving 99x = 27, so x = 3/11.

title: Three cones fill a cylinder
line: Side views of a cone and cylinder with the same base and height: the cone pours three times and the cylinder fills exactly.

title: Distance by a hidden triangle
line: Points (1, 2) and (7, 10) sprout a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, and the hypotenuse measures 10.

title: Every point 5 away
line: A point sweeps around the origin at distance 5, and each time it hits a grid point like (3, 4) a right triangle flashes.

title: Sliding ladder
line: A 13-foot ladder slides down a wall, and when its foot is 5 feet out, a right triangle shows the top at 12 feet.

title: Pythagoras by rearranging
line: Four copies of a right triangle sit inside a big square, then slide around so the empty space changes from c² into a² + b².

title: Tiles refill the big square
line: Squares on legs 3 and 4 break into unit tiles that fly over and exactly refill the 5 by 5 square on the hypotenuse.

title: The converse on a hinge
line: Sticks of 3 and 4 hinged together open until the gap between their ends is exactly 5, and the angle reads 90 degrees.

title: Torn corners make a line
line: A triangle's three corners tear off and slide together along a line, fitting exactly into a straight 180 degree angle.

title: Sliding transversal
line: A transversal crosses two parallel lines and tilts back and forth, and its eight angles only ever show two values that add to 180.

title: Exterior angle filled
line: One side of a triangle extends past a corner, and the two far angles slide over to exactly fill the outside angle.

title: Two angles are enough
line: Two triangles with angles 30 and 70 start at different sizes, and one dilates until it lands exactly on the other.

title: Dilate, turn, land
line: A small triangle dilates by 2 from a center point, turns 90 degrees, and slides to land exactly on a larger triangle.

title: Moves with live coordinates
line: A triangle on a grid reflects, rotates, and dilates while its corner coordinates update live: (x, y) to (−x, y) to (2x, 2y).

title: Rotating swaps coordinates
line: Point (3, 1) rotates 90 degrees around the origin to (−1, 3), and a triangle traced through it turns along with it.

title: Snapping one shape onto another
line: Two matching arrow shapes sit on a plane, and the first slides, turns 120 degrees, then flips to snap exactly onto the second.

title: Rotations keep everything
line: Two parallel segments rotate around a point, and live readouts show their lengths and the angle between them never change.
